title: Handle account-exists-with-different-credential and credential-already-in-use for the Google sign-in / link-provider paths

evidence.quote:
final localMatch = await registry.findByEmail(googleUser.email ?? '');
      if (localMatch != null && localMatch.accountTier.isLocal) {

why: A repo-wide grep for 'account-exists-with-different-credential' and 'credential-already-in-use' returns zero hits anywhere in lib/. A user who already has a password-based Firebase account under an email and taps 'Sign in with Google' (or 'Link Google' in Settings) using the same address will hit one of these two Firebase codes; neither auth_repository_impl.dart's Google methods nor either screen's _mapAuthError switch has a case for them, so both fall to the generic default branch ('Sign-in failed' / 'Google sign-in failed') with zero guidance to use the existing password and no merge option — unlike the parallel email-already-in-use case in upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart, which has a complete EmailCollisionException-driven merge flow (executeUploadLocalIntoCloud / executeKeepCloudDiscardLocal). AU-2 explicitly names both codes as requiring an explicit merge flow.
recommendation: Add both codes to both _mapAuthError switches with an actionable message ('this email already has a password — sign in that way'), and extend the merge machinery upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart already has for the password path to cover the Google-credential collision (e.g. capture the pending OAuth credential, prompt for the existing password, then link).
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: stub the auth gateway to throw account-exists-with-different-credential from signInWithGoogle(), assert SignInController/SignupScreen surface a specific actionable message (not the generic fallback).
Regression test: same for credential-already-in-use thrown from linkGoogleProvider().

refutations: AU-2's text/"why" scope it to the linkWithCredential/offline-merge flow (protecting anonymous users' data during AU-1 conversion), sourced from Firebase's account-linking docs. All 3 cited evidence sites (auth_repository_impl.dart:47 signInWithGoogle, sign_in_controller.dart:114, signup_screen.dart:
corrections: Drop credential-already-in-use and the "'Link Google' in Settings" claim — linkGoogleProvider() has no UI caller (dead code), and that code is genuinely uninstrumented but currently unreachable, so it carries no user-visible severity today. The real, reachable gap is narrower: account-exists-with-different-credential falls to the generic default branch in sign_in_controller.dart:114 and signup_screen.dart:488 for a user whose email already has a password account and taps "Sign in with Google" — poor UX, but no data-loss risk (not an offline/anonymous conversion), so AU-2's "never drop offline data" rationale doesn't transfer; this is closer to a message-quality/EH-5-adjacent gap than a violated AU-2 invariant.

The actual 'on link' code path AU-2 targets (linkGoogleProvider/linkWithGoogleIdToken) has zero call sites in lib/ outside the repository/service layer — no Settings screen wires it to a button, so the 'Link Google in Settings' scenario is unreachable in the shipped app. The 3 evidence lines are all plain signInWithCredential sign-in/sign-up paths, and 'credential-already-in-use' cannot occur there since that code is link-exclusive.

The finding's why-section claims a user can hit this via 'Link Google in Settings' — no such UI exists; linkGoogleProvider()/linkWithGoogleIdToken (auth_repository_impl.dart:133-136, account_management_service.dart:155-157) have no callers anywhere under lib/features/settings/presentation or lib/features/account/presentation (grep confirms only test callers), so that path is dead code, not a live site. The 3 cited evidence lines themselves are accurate and reachable (verified via signInWithGoogle at sign_in_controller.dart:849-970 and _signUpWithGoogle at signup_screen.dart:329-465, both funnelling unmatched Firebase codes into the default branch).

mergedFrom: Local-born-account Google-collision detector can never match now that offline accounts use synthetic emails
